headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared channel or write overlap is documented, but ComfyUI’s file-based model surfaces create a small prompt-injection and leakage surface if paired with a file-consuming workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can read model/workflow files and uses an asynchronous queue, but spring-integration-samples has no documented input surface or output channel that would automatically feed into it. The pair lacks a shared channel by default, so only unusual manual bridging would enable injection.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated content into a ComfyUI workflow or prompt file, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two, B content can reach A without provenance checks.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste B outputs into ComfyUI prompt/workflow files without review.
Disable any shared folder mounts between the two.
Add a short provenance note to any manually transferred text.
requires-engineering: add content-signing or provenance tagging on transferred artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches local model and workflow files, while spring-integration-samples is documented with no data classes touched and no network egress. There is no documented shared workspace or third-party upload path, so leakage is limited unless an operator introduces shared files containing sensitive content.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, files opened by A could be exposed to B through manual handling.
IF sensitive images or workflows are copied into B’s environment, they may be retained outside A’s controls.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Avoid placing sensitive images or workflows in shared locations.
Review any exported artifacts before moving them between agents.
Delete temporary transfer files after use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI has no filesystem write, shell, or git modification capability, and spring-integration-samples is not runnable and exposes no write or mutable-resource scopes. With no overlapping write surface, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible from the profiles provided.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to grant shared write access to the same directory, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
IF spring-integration-samples becomes runnable with mutable resource access, overlap could emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only relative to shared assets.
Do not grant git or filesystem write permissions to either agent.
Recheck the pair if B becomes runnable.
Document any future shared mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI produces workflows and generated media, but spring-integration-samples is not runnable and has no documented downstream action-taking authority. Without an execution path, B cannot automatically treat A’s output as authoritative, so cascading error is limited to manual misuse.
conditions: IF an operator manually uses ComfyUI outputs as inputs to a separate automation, errors can cascade.
IF B is later made runnable and consumes A outputs without verification, the risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing A outputs.
Label generated artifacts as unverified.
Do not wire A outputs directly into any automation.
Keep B non-runnable unless a verification step is added.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency constraint, or retention policy mismatch is documented for either agent. ComfyUI is open-source and offline-capable, while spring-integration-samples has no data classes touched or permissions requested, so no compliance breach pathway is evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data, compliance review must be redone.
IF a residency or retention policy is introduced for either agent, the pair should be reassessed.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair.
Record any future data residency requirements.
Review retention settings before deployment.
Keep offline processing for A where possible.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement if regulated data is introduced.
